title: Reservoirized SLO Stream Limiter with KV Urgency Decay
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build a reservoir-based SLO-aware stream limiter that enforces tenant fairness while minimizing KV cache churn and GPU memory pressure. The feature introduces a per-tenant reservoir of admission tokens that are consumed by incoming continuous-batching streams. Token replenishment is shaped by tenant SLO class, recent completion latency, and a KV urgency-decay score that biases reservations towards hot state tenants to reduce expensive KV refills. The goal is to reduce tail latency violations under high concurrency while preserving KV cache locality and avoiding aggressive global evictions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under mixed workload stress tests, P95 latency for P0 tenants is within target SLOs and no more than 3x baseline KV miss rate increase; 2) End-to-end throughput does not regress more than 8% for best-effort tenants when limiters are active; 3) Metrics emitted for reservoir occupancy, KV urgency, preemption count, and eviction-induced misses; 4) Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolled out to canary region with automated rollback on error budget burn >10%.
design_decisions:
- Use per-tenant reservoir tokens (short-lived credits) instead of strict slot preemption to provide soft isolation and reduce churn.
- Compute token refill rate as a weighted function of tenant SLO tier, recent latency deficit (EMA of lateness), and KV urgency-decay score.
- KV urgency-decay: an exponential decay score that rises when a tenant triggers a KV miss and decays as cache hits occur; higher urgency increases token refill priority.
- Eviction policy: prefer compacting cold segments first and limit full-slab evictions; incorporate urgency to avoid evicting hotsets.
- Preemption model: if reservoir depleted, new streams are delayed up to a short soft-window (50-200ms) before preemptive termination; allow resumable streams with preserved KV pointers where possible.
- Minimal changes to public API: behavior is internal to runtime; expose observability hooks and per-tenant admin knobs in Console.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime components: reservoir manager, urgency scorer, compressor for KV segments, and admission path hooks.
- Reservoir manager holds small integer credits per tenant, persisted in-memory with bounded memory cost.
- Urgency scorer maintains EMA with tau=30s and score scaled to [0,1]. Score bump on KV miss events and on latency violations.
- Admission path: before a new batch select, check reservoir; if credits available, decrement and allow; if not, consult soft-backoff window and urgency to decide delay vs preempt.
- KV bookkeeping: add per-tenant hotset fingerprint and last-touch timestamps to guide compact-eviction.
- GPU memory: add fast compaction trigger when device free memory < 12% to avoid OOM; compaction prioritized for non-urgent tenants.
- Config flags: runtime.feature.reservoirized_limiter, runtime.param.reservoir_size_default, runtime.param.soft_window_ms.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for reservoir state machine and urgency-decay math.
- Microbench harness: synthetic latency-shaped workloads to verify refill responsiveness and fairness.
- Replay tests: run production traces against a scaled-down cluster to measure KV miss delta and P95 latency.
- Chaos: force KV miss storms and memory pressure to validate compaction path and preemption decisions.
- Performance regression: compare throughput/latency against baseline across 1000-simulated tenants.
- Integration: enable on canary cluster with BETA tenants and monitor burn rates for 72h.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag + unit/integration tests. 2) Deploy to canary pool (5% capacity) and route 2% production traffic for 48h. 3) If stable, progressive rollout to 25% then 50% with automated gates measuring P95, eviction-rate, and error budget. 4) Full rollout if metrics stable for 7d; otherwise rollback to previous flag state. 5) Post-rollout: monitor for 30d and iterate on refill parameters.
risks:
- Mis-tuned refill weights can starve best-effort tenants or under-protect high-tier SLOs.
- Urgency scoring might overreact to transient KV misses and lock tokens to a tenant, reducing global throughput.
- Compaction under pressure could introduce CPU overhead impacting latency.
- Incorrect preservation of resumable stream state could lead to KV pointer inconsistencies.
- Operational complexity: too many knobs exposed could confuse SREs.
metrics:
- reservoir.tokens.available (per-tenant)
- reservoir.refill.rate (per-tenant)
- reservoir.preemption.count
- kv.urgency.score (per-tenant)
- kv.evictions.by_type (compact|slab_full)
- gpu.memory.free_pct
- latency.p95, latency.p99 (per-tenant tier)
- throughput.requests/sec (global and per-tier)
comments: 2026-02-22 - Priya Kapoor: Initial writeup and rationale. Put up design doc link. Asked runtime and KV owners for feasibility review.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Reviewed design; requested clarifications on token integer overflow and persistence across worker restarts. Proposed to cap reservoir at 1024 and treat as ephemeral (no durable store).

2026-03-02 - Marissa Lee (KV team): Suggested adding per-segment last-touch fingerprint to avoid hotset evictions; flagged compaction CPU cost risk. Added acceptance criteria for <3x KV miss increase.

2026-03-05 - Diego Morales: Prototype implemented basic reservoir manager and urgency scorer. Local microbench shows 18% reduction in P99 violations for priority tenants under mixed load. Attached PR for early review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1589
2026-03-09 - SRE: Run replay on staging traces; found GPU free_pct dips under heavy cold workloads causing compaction thrashing. Added temporary guard to delay compaction if latency spike detected.
2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor: Updated ticket with adjusted soft_window_ms from 100 to 200ms after Diego's observation that short waits reduced overall eviction churn. Planning canary rollout next week.
2026-03-12 - QA: Added integration test cases to simulate resumable stream failure and KV pointer consistency; initial runs pass on CI with minor flakiness (investigating).
